method.prompts_source: dev.benchmarks.draft_comparison.PROMPTS; Qwen token IDs in TranscriptPrompts.hpp
method.censoring: Exclude each request final cycle, then exclude any remaining cycle that verifies fewer than seven proposals. Conditional acceptance counts cycles reaching each position; survival uses all eligible cycles.
method.timing_scope: Not a throughput comparison; no ABBA order or quietness trace for this acceptance study.

prompts.fibonacci: Write a Python function that returns the nth Fibonacci number using iteration. Return only the function.
prompts.merge_sort: Implement a stable merge sort in Python. Include a short explanation of its complexity.
prompts.lru_cache: Write a Python LRU cache using a doubly linked list and a dictionary. Explain invariants briefly.
prompts.typescript_retry: Write a TypeScript function that retries an asynchronous operation with exponential backoff.

comparison.method: Full-width cycles only; final cycle excluded conservatively for EOS/output-cap censoring. This is an acceptance study, not a speed comparison.

interpretation: The LRU gap is not a worse first-proposal rejection rate: DSpine rejects 3/51 eligible first proposals versus DFlash2 4/45. In this short trace its losses are larger at positions 2 and 6.
Merge sort shows lower conditional survival especially at positions 5 and 7 in this short trace.
Fibonacci saturates the seven-proposal cap in 10/12 eligible cycles for both drafters. Native sixteen-row execution is worth measuring on such continuations.
A longer block can extend full accepted prefixes, but these fractions do not predict its speedup or the acceptance of later positions.
BF16 draft precision and native sixteen-row execution have not been measured; neither is established as the cause of the current acceptance gap.
